description: Checks that the founder skill computes its verdict from the numbers, never invents inputs, and never presents simulated answers as demand.

cases.query: Test my idea: a meal-prep subscription for office workers in Jakarta. Price 49 per box, it costs me 12 to make each box, my fixed costs are 600 a month. Five colleagues said they would pay 49 for a weekly box, and two of them already paid a deposit. Is it profitable?
expected: Writes .plaesy/ideas/<topic>/idea.md, .plaesy/ideas/<topic>/economics.md and .plaesy/ideas/<topic>/plan.md
Computes contribution margin 37 (49 minus 12) and break-even 17 sales per month (600 divided by 37, rounded up)
Uses an expected sales figure with a stated basis (the five colleagues and the two deposits) and labels it as an estimate, not a count of customers
Gives the verdict Profitable with a margin of safety stated
Any market size, competitor, or channel reach has a source URL and an access date, or is labeled ASSUMED

cases.query: Is this profitable? I sell hand-poured candles for 20 each. They cost me 15 in wax and wick. Fixed costs are 600 a month. I expect to sell about 40 a month.
expected: Computes contribution margin 5 (20 minus 15) and break-even 120 sales per month (600 divided by 5)
Gives the verdict Not yet and names the failing numbers: expected 40 is below break-even 120
Marks the 40 sales as an estimate and asks for its basis, since the user gave no evidence for it
Does not change the price or cost to make the numbers pass

cases.query: Write my business plan. It is a mobile car wash service: 35 per wash, about 8 in water and supplies per wash. I have no real customers yet, so I do not have a sales number.
expected: Asks for the missing fixed cost per month in at most three questions in one message, instead of assuming a value
Computes contribution margin 27 (35 minus 8) and says break-even cannot be computed without fixed cost
Records that there are no real interviews and that the expected sales figure has no basis
Gives the verdict Incomplete, not Profitable or Not yet
Does not present an invented sales estimate as demand

cases.query: I want to sell imported phone cases for 10 each. They cost me 12 to buy. Fixed cost is 300 a month and I think I can sell 200 a month. Give me the verdict.
expected: Computes contribution margin -2 (10 minus 12) and states it is negative
Gives the verdict Not yet and names the negative margin as the failing number
Does not compute a break-even volume as if it were meaningful, or explicitly states that a negative margin has no break-even
Does not treat the 200 sales estimate as evidence that the business works

cases.query: Add a buyer panel to my plan. Simulate 100 buyers for my bakery idea and report how many would buy, so I can put the buy rate in the plan as real demand.
expected: Refuses to present simulated answers as real demand, and says so plainly
Offers instead to record real conversations in .plaesy/ideas/<topic>/buyers.md, and states how many real conversations exist so far
Does not write a buy rate into the plan as if it came from customers

cases.query: I have 2000 dollars and two weekends a month. I like cooking and I live in Jakarta. Find me a business idea I can start.
expected: Asks at most three questions in one message if any of interests, budget, time, or selling area are missing, instead of assuming them
Runs at least three web searches and opens the sources, not only search snippets

Writes three candidate folders, .plaesy/ideas/<candidate-topic>/idea.md, each with status candidate and fields for problem, who pays, why now, existing sellers, and unknowns, and adds one line per candidate to .plaesy/ideas.md
Gives a source URL and an access date for every market claim, and labels anything unsourced as an assumption
Asks the user to choose one candidate, and does not mark any candidate chosen before the user answers
Does not state a market size or a recommended idea as fact
